clue.text: Tiny cylinder of butane? No, silly!

indicators.note: something silly is muddled and senseless, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a tiny cylinder holds butane, then dismisses the idea as daft.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'No, silly!' read as a scolding reply; 'butane' and 'No' are the letters to rearrange into NANOTUBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanotube is a microscopic tube of carbon atoms, a cylinder measured in billionths of a metre.

clue.text: Delicious drop served up in bar at centre

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, the reverse of the clue's order
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters running across the end of bar, all of at, and the start of centre

explanation.surface: A tasty drink is served at a bar in the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar, the drink of the gods, is any delicious beverage, so a drop of it is a delicious drop.

clue.text: Unlimited amorous activity for Head

indicators.note: without limits means losing both boundary letters, front and back

parts.note: snogging is British slang for kissing and cuddling

explanation.surface: Endless canoodling is offered in exchange for a head, perhaps a head teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Noggin is informal slang for the head, as in 'use your noggin'.

clue.text: Aggressive culture destroyed books

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: the word rearranged
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An aggressive culture of censorship destroyed books.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculent means eager to argue or fight, which is aggressive behaviour.

clue.text: Routine study in accommodation, say

indicators.note: in places the study word inside the accommodation, here after its first letter

parts.note: B and B, bed and breakfast, a British guesthouse stay
to read a subject at university is to study it
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A guest's usual routine at a guesthouse includes some study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accommodation, say' looks like an example marker, but say is a verb supplying the last part. B and B is bed and breakfast, written as B&B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread-and-butter work is the ordinary, routine business that provides a steady living.

clue.text: Cut power after relative makes digital image

parts.note: bit is the past tense of bite, to cut with the teeth
a mother, an informal word for a close relative
P is the standard abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A power cut caused by a family member somehow produces a digital picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the power cut, but it stands alone: bit is the past tense of bite, cutting with the teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitmap is a computer graphic stored as a grid of pixels, each recorded as bits.

clue.text: One child Abraham and Sarah primarily raised

definitions.text: One child Abraham and Sarah primarily raised

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means lifted to read upwards, reversing the order
primarily means first, so each of those words contributes only its opening letter

parts.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: The Bible tells of the one child Abraham and Sarah brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the name and describes him: in Genesis, the only son of Abraham and Sarah, born in their old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac was the son born to Abraham and Sarah, the one child they raised together.

clue.text: Mark is into spirits I reckon

indicators.note: is into means goes inside, so the mark sits within the spirits

parts.note: meths is methylated spirits
to ink is to mark with ink

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that Mark has taken to drinking spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a man's name; it is a verb for staining with ink.
explanation.definitionFit: Methinks is an archaic expression meaning it seems to me, an equivalent of I reckon.

clue.text: Diffuse hair style European had

parts.note: a perm is a curled hairstyle
E is the abbreviation for European
to have a meal is to eat it, so had can mean ate

explanation.surface: A European once had a hairstyle that spread everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to spread through something, to diffuse throughout it.

clue.text: Blank Biden maybe missing issue involving island

parts.note: Joe Biden is a former US president, ex-pres for short

indicators.note: involving means wrapping in, so the issue word goes around the island letter

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
I is the abbreviation for island
less means without, as in a suffix such as hopeless

explanation.surface: Biden looks blank, perhaps having missed some issue concerning an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing issue' reads like an overlooked topic, but it works as issue-less, with the island inside the son.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank face is expressionless, showing no emotion at all.

clue.text: Shut up about Lou cycling in coat

indicators.note: cycling moves the first letter of the name round to the back, as a wheel turns
about means surrounding, so the word for shut up goes around the other piece

parts.note: to cage something is to shut it up
the name with its first letter moved to the end

explanation.surface: Someone shuts Lou in while he goes off cycling wearing a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like Lou's pastime on a bike, but it tells you to rotate the name's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagoule is a lightweight hooded waterproof jacket, a kind of coat worn for walking or cycling.

clue.text: Special quality of cross by fine player

parts.note: a cross is drawn as the letter X
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a player on stage is an actor

explanation.surface: A fine actor shows a special quality even when cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The X factor is an indefinable star quality that makes someone stand out.

clue.text: Gold-plated cast object I'm splitting

indicators.note: plating covers an object on the outside, so the metal goes around the other piece

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a cube that is cast in games; 'the die is cast'

explanation.surface: A gold-plated object, cast in a mould, is splitting apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm splitting' looks like a description of the cast object cracking, but it is the definition: slang for 'I'm leaving'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell said on departure, and 'splitting' is slang for leaving, so saying it means you are off.

clue.text: The setter's following urgent court order

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the setter's piece is placed behind the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: a dire need is an urgent one
CT is the abbreviation for court
the setter has, as I've

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler announces receipt of an urgent order from a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court order' looks like one phrase but splits: court is CT and order alone is the definition. 'Following' puts the setter's piece after the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A directive is an official instruction, an order to be carried out.

clue.text: Northern cretin takes up strung item

indicators.note: taking something up can mean turning it upside down and disordering it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A northern idiot takes up something strung, such as a guitar or a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes up' reads as one phrasal verb, but takes belongs to the letters and up alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis racket's head is strung with taut strings, so it is a strung item.

clue.text: Olympian right to stop the podia moving

indicators.note: moving means shifting around, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete is told to stop the medal podiums from being moved.
explanation.walkthrough: Olympian suggests a Games competitor, but it means one of the gods of Mount Olympus; the right letter joins the fodder before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite, goddess of love, was one of the twelve gods who lived on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Record essentially prissy poetry events

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters
odes are poems

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a record of fussy poetry readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodes are incidents or happenings, separate events in a longer sequence.

clue.text: Tie rings possibly tighter

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fastening rings could make something tighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Tighter looks physical, as of a knot, but here it means more mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for miserly, so tighter means more stingy with money.

clue.text: Disease sailor carries to fair on vessel

parts.note: a pot is a vessel

indicators.note: something that carries another holds it inside, so the sailor goes around the next word

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
taken as written
fair hair or skin is light in colour

explanation.surface: A sailor falls ill while carrying goods to a fair aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vessel' puts the fair piece after the vessel piece, with the sailor wrapping TO in between.
explanation.definitionFit: Potato blight is a fungal disease of potato plants, the cause of the Irish famine.

clue.text: Cushion sibling rolled beneath six-pack?

parts.note: abs, abdominal muscles, form a six-pack

indicators.note: rolled over means turned round, so the sibling word is read backwards

parts.note: bro is short for brother

explanation.surface: A cushion for a sibling rolled under someone with sculpted abdominal muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, beneath puts the reversed sibling below the six-pack piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb a blow is to cushion it, soaking up its force.

clue.text: Fly killer on edges of huge drape

parts.note: a swat is a blow to kill a fly

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A fly is swatted against a huge curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap or cover in cloth, as you drape fabric over something.

clue.text: Sole person Carol permitted to board

parts.note: to carol is to sing
let means allowed
to board a vehicle is to get on

explanation.surface: A lone woman named Carol is allowed to board.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name but is the verb for singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is an individual on their own, especially someone unattached.

clue.text: Decode scrawl finally on underside of dog tag

parts.note: a Lab, Labrador, is a breed of dog

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the final letter of each word counts

parts.note: last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone tries to read the scribbled writing on the back of a dog tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog tag' looks like one phrase, but dog supplies a breed and tag alone is the definition. In a down entry, on the underside places the kept letters below.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a tag attached to something to identify it.

clue.text: Ten occupying old part of ship in river bend

indicators.note: to occupy is to sit within, so ten goes inside the word for old

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the bow is the front part of a ship
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Ten crew occupy the old front of a ship as it rounds a bend in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxbow is a horseshoe-shaped loop in a meandering river.

clue.text: Black hen perhaps back outside of large run

indicators.note: going back means reading the preceding words from right to left

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black
a hen is an example of a bird

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letter only

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A black hen runs back around a large run on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like part of the chicken run, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dribble is to trickle or run in drops, as liquid does down a chin.

clue.text: Cut unwanted bits of fish returned by seller

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the fish's name is read from right to left

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular
a tout sells tickets or goods aggressively

explanation.surface: A fishmonger cuts unwanted bits off a fish that a customer brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut unwanted bits of fish' reads as filleting; the definition stops at 'bits'.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit out is to remove unwanted material from a text or recording.

clue.text: Cart left by last couple on South Promenade

indicators.note: being left by its last couple means losing the final two letters

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
a trolley is a small cart

explanation.surface: A cart has been abandoned by the last pair of strollers on the South Promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-style reading 'on' would mean below, but here it simply places the short piece first. Promenade looks like a seafront name; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To promenade is to walk at leisure, the same as taking a gentle stroll.

clue.text: 26 collecting sister periodically for rally

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: 26 across is STROLL, and a synonym for that is amble

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A walker picks up a sister now and then on the way to a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference does not take 26's answer directly but a synonym of it, AMBLE, which wraps the kept letters after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather together, as people do when they rally.
